newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 12.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp is expected to announce on Tuesday it will spin off of its industrial units into a company, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Other top stories included:
- HFS Inc will buy PHH Corp for stock valued at $1.7 billion or $49.50 a share.
- U.S. investigators are trying to find out if Texaco Inc executives withheld or destroyed documents sought in a racial discrimination suit.
- General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co reduced their fourth-period vehicle-output plans from a month ago.
- The U.S. chip industry's book-to-bill indicator rose to 1.10 in October, the highest level this year.
- IBM Corp and Siemens AG are getting together to create an Internet-based system for buying and selling electric capacity.
- Hughes Electronics Corp is consolidating the company's efforts to expand DirecTV satellite-to-home services around the world.
- Bergen Brunswig and IVAX Corp shares fell as investors were not pleased with their planned merger.
- The NASDAQ ended in record territory in light trading at 1,262.67.
- Vanguard Chairman Bogle criticized what he called mutual-fund "supermarkets," saying they promoted "casino capitalism."
- Computer software retailer NeoStar Retail Group Inc will auction off its stores.
- Japan's prime minister has called on his cabinet to change regulations governing the country's financial markets.
- Glaxo Wellcome Plc's new AIDS drug will not likely get to the market before mid-1998.
- Deutsche Telekom AG got permission to increase its initial public offering by 20 percent.
- Italy will merge state-owned holding company Stet with its main operating susidiary, Telecom Italia.
- Olivetti's stock rose 4.8 percent following news that the company sold stake in a cellular-phone venture.
- Merrill Lynch plans to buy Australia's McIntosh Securities for $94 million.
- Marshall Cogan must show he can prosper among the competitive car dealership chains after his United Auto Group Inc made an initial public offering.
- WR Lazard & Co has named Marianne Spraggins as its chief executive officer. Spraggins was the managing director at Smith Barney Inc.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
